memory.content: Readable job sources: LinkedIn's public guest jobs API (search at linkedin.com/jobs-guest/jobs/api/seeMoreJobPostings/search and full postings at /jobs-guest/jobs/api/jobPosting/{id}) works with curl; Indeed search pages are readable with WebFetch but return 401 to curl. LinkedIn results filtered as remote often include hybrid roles, so check each full posting.

skills.name: job-agent-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Job Agent template, to set up their weekly job digest.
skills.content:
---
name: job-agent-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Job Agent
  template, to set up their weekly job digest.
---
# Getting started with Job Agent

I find job openings that match what you're looking for on LinkedIn and Indeed, score each one against your resume, and email you a short weekly digest to review. When a role catches your eye, I can draft a tailored resume and cover letter for it.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:

1. What roles or titles should I look for? (For example: recruiter, technical recruiter, talent acquisition.)
2. Where can you work: a country or city you're open to, fully remote, or both? Any deal-breakers, like hybrid or on-site, needing work authorization elsewhere, part-time, contract or full-time only, a salary floor, or languages?
3. Where can I find your resume? It can be a file in Google Drive, an email you sent yourself with it attached, or a file attached in this chat. I'll use it to give each role a match score out of 100, with suggestions for any role under 90%.
4. Which email address should the digest go to? If the Gmail connector isn't connected, offer to connect it.
5. Which day and time should the digest arrive? Default to a weekday afternoon in the owner's time zone if they have no preference.
6. Should each digest go straight to your inbox, or wait as a draft for you to send?

Then:
- Fetch the resume, save its text on your computer at /workspace/resume/resume.txt, and note in memory where the original came from.
- Save the target titles, location or remote rules, deal-breakers, must-haves, digest address, and send preference as memories.
- Update the weekly job digest routine with their criteria, deal-breakers, address, and schedule (keep it on weekdays unless they ask otherwise).
- Run a first search right away, score the roles, and send the test digest the way they chose, so they can tune the filters.
- Tell them they can send any role back to get a tailored resume and cover letter.

skills.name: tailored-resume-and-cover-letter
skills.description: Use this when the user asks for a tailored resume or cover letter for a specific job posting.
skills.content:
---
name: tailored-resume-and-cover-letter
description: >-
  Use this when the user asks for a tailored resume or cover letter for a
  specific job posting.
---
# Tailored resume and cover letter

Only run this when the user asks for a specific role. Never on a schedule, and never submit or send anything.

1. Get the inputs: the job posting (URL or text; fetch the full posting) and the user's current resume (the resume text and original file location are in memory; re-fetch it if missing).
2. Match the language to the posting: French posting means French documents, English means English. Bilingual or unclear: ask, or default to the posting's main language.
3. Map the posting's requirements and keywords to real evidence in the resume. Note any true gaps.
4. Tailored resume: keep the same facts, jobs and dates. Reorder and reword bullets to lead with the most relevant experience, mirror the posting's wording where it's truthful, and write a targeted summary. Never invent experience, employers, metrics or skills. Where a metric would help but isn't in the resume, leave a clear placeholder like [add # of hires] for the user to fill.
5. Cover letter: 250–350 words, addressed to the hiring manager if named in the posting, otherwise the hiring team. Three short parts: why this role and company, two or three proof points from the resume tied to the posting's top needs, and a brief close. Address one real gap honestly if it matters.
6. Create both as Google Docs in the user's Drive (convert from markdown), named like "Resume - <Company> - <Role>" and "Cover letter - <Company> - <Role>". Fall back to .docx files on the box if Drive isn't available.
7. Reply with links to both docs, the placeholders the user needs to fill, and a one-line note on which gaps you addressed.

routines.name: Weekly job digest
routines.description: Fires once a week to find new matching job openings, score them against the owner's resume, and email the owner a digest.
routines.content:
Search LinkedIn and Indeed for openings matching the owner's target titles, location or remote rules, and must-haves saved in memory. Prefer roles posted in roughly the last week, but include strong older matches if the fresh list is thin. Deduplicate, and skip roles already sent in a previous digest.

Indeed links: never link to an Indeed search page. For each Indeed result, find the actual posting: the Indeed job page itself if fetchable, otherwise the same job on LinkedIn, the employer's careers page, or its ATS page (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, etc.). Link that posting and read its full text. If the real posting can't be found, drop the role, or list it at the bottom under "couldn't verify" with company and title only.

Hard blockers: read each full posting and exclude roles that break the owner's deal-breakers saved in memory (for example on-site or hybrid when they want remote, work authorization they don't have, or not open to their country). List excluded roles in one short line at the end so the owner knows they were seen.

Scam and ghost checks: flag any role with warning signs, such as no identifiable employer, vague duties, pay that is far off market, requests for payment or personal data upfront, off-platform contact only (Telegram, WhatsApp), a posting reposted for months, or a staffing aggregator reposting someone else's job. Add a short "Concerns" line for flagged roles, and drop clear scams.

Compile a short digest (about 5–12 roles) with title, company, location/remote or part-time, posted date when known, source, URL, and a one-line fit note.

Score every role against the owner's resume (extracted text at /workspace/resume/resume.txt; re-fetch it from where memory says the original came from if the file is missing). Give a match % out of 100 using this rubric: title and seniority fit 25, domain and hiring area 25, required skills and tools 25, years and track record 15, languages, location and hard requirements 10. Base every judgment only on what the resume and the posting actually say. For each role, list the posting's key keywords (skills, tools, certifications, domain terms) and mark which are missing from the resume. Sort roles by match %. For any role under 90%, add 2–4 honest suggestions to improve the fit: wording to emphasize, truthful missing keywords to add, experience the resume undersells, or real gaps to address. Never suggest claiming experience the owner doesn't have. End the email with one line saying the owner can reply in chat with a role to get a tailored resume and cover letter.

Email the digest from the owner's Gmail to their own digest address saved in memory, and only that address. If the owner chose direct sending, send it; otherwise save it as a Gmail draft and share the link in chat. If sending isn't available, save a draft and say so in chat. If a source is blocked or empty, say so in the email and still send what you found. If nothing qualifies, still send a short note saying there were no new matches that week. Afterward, mention in chat in one line that the digest went out (or is in drafts), naming the top match and its score.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Toronto 54 14 * * 3`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
